title: Constitutional Referendum Restores Multiparty Democracy
description: A constitutional referendum on 12 July 1991 approved a new constitution restoring multiparty politics for the first time since the 1960s, creating a bicameral parliament. Approved by 98% of voters, it established the framework for competitive elections under President Taya's military-turned-civilian regime.

title: Taya Wins First Multiparty Presidential Election
description: President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya won Mauritania's first multiparty presidential election in January 1992, legitimizing his rule after seizing power in a 1984 coup. Opposition candidates alleged widespread fraud and the results were disputed, setting a pattern for contested elections.

title: US Suspends Aid Over Human Rights Concerns
description: The United States suspended development assistance to Mauritania citing persistent human rights violations including forced labor, ethnic discrimination against Black Mauritanians, and restrictions on political freedoms. The suspension signaled growing international scrutiny of the Taya regime.

title: SOS Esclaves Anti-Slavery Organization Founded
description: Activists secretly founded SOS Esclaves (SOS Slaves) in 1995 to document and combat the persistence of chattel slavery in Mauritania despite its formal abolition in 1981. The organization became a critical voice exposing the gap between legal abolition and continued enslavement of Haratine communities.

title: Taya Re-elected in Boycotted Presidential Election
description: President Taya won re-election with over 90% of the vote after major opposition parties boycotted the December 1997 presidential election. The boycott reflected deep distrust in the electoral process and consolidated Taya's authoritarian grip on power.

title: Mauritania Establishes Diplomatic Relations with Israel
description: Mauritania became the third Arab League member after Egypt and Jordan to establish full diplomatic relations with Israel, signing the agreement in Washington on 28 October 1999. The move was deeply controversial domestically and across the Arab world, drawing protests and accusations of betraying the Palestinian cause.

title: Failed Coup Attempt Against Taya Regime
description: Military officers launched an unsuccessful coup attempt against President Taya in June 2000, reflecting growing dissatisfaction within the armed forces. The failed putsch led to a crackdown on suspected dissidents and tightened security around the presidency.

title: Chinguetti Offshore Oil Field Discovered
description: Australian firm Woodside Petroleum discovered Mauritania's first commercial oil field, Chinguetti, in deepwater offshore in May 2001. Estimated at 123 million barrels, the discovery raised hopes for an oil-fueled economic transformation and attracted international investment interest.

title: Second Failed Coup Attempt and Military Crackdown
description: A more serious coup attempt in June 2003 involved heavy fighting in Nouakchott over two days before loyalist forces prevailed. President Taya responded with mass arrests of military officers and Islamist activists, deepening political repression.

title: Taya Wins Third Term Amid Fraud Allegations
description: President Taya won a third presidential term in November 2003 with 67% of the vote in an election marred by opposition allegations of ballot-stuffing and voter intimidation. The contested result further delegitimized civilian governance under military-backed rule.

title: GSPC Attack on Lemgheity Military Base
description: The Algerian Salafist Group for Preaching and Combat (GSPC) attacked a remote army barracks at Lemgheity on 4 June 2005, killing 15 Mauritanian soldiers in the deadliest terrorist attack in the country's history. The assault exposed Mauritania's vulnerability to Saharan jihadist groups and marked the beginning of a six-year terror campaign.

title: Military Coup Overthrows President Taya
description: The Military Council for Justice and Democracy (CMJD) overthrew President Taya in a bloodless coup on 3 August 2005 while he attended a Saudi funeral. Colonel Ely Ould Mohamed Vall led the junta, which promised a democratic transition within two years.

title: Constitutional Referendum Limits Presidential Terms
description: A constitutional referendum on 25 June 2006 was approved by 97% of voters, imposing a two-term limit on the presidency and reducing terms from six to five years. The reform also set a maximum age of 75 for presidential candidates, establishing guardrails for the democratic transition.

title: First Oil Production from Chinguetti Field
description: Oil production began at the Chinguetti field in February 2006, making Mauritania an oil-producing nation for the first time. However, reserves were quickly downgraded from 123 to 53 million barrels by November 2006, dampening expectations of an oil boom.

title: First Fully Democratic Presidential Election
description: Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi won Mauritania's first genuinely democratic presidential election on 25 March 2007 in a runoff, marking the transfer from military to civilian rule. International observers deemed the election free and fair, representing a milestone in the country's political development.

title: Anti-Slavery Law Criminalizes Slaveholding
description: Under international pressure, Mauritania's parliament passed a law in August 2007 making slaveholding a criminal offense punishable by up to 10 years in prison. Despite the legislation, enforcement remained minimal and slavery continued to affect an estimated 1-4% of the population.

title: AQIM Murders French Tourists in Aleg
description: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) gunmen killed four French tourists near the town of Aleg in December 2007, marking the group's first attack on Western civilians in Mauritania. The attack devastated the nascent tourism sector and led to the cancellation of the Dakar Rally.

title: Military Coup Ousts Elected President Abdallahi
description: General Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz led a military coup on 6 August 2008 that ousted President Abdallahi after just 15 months in office, following a dispute over military appointments. The coup was widely condemned internationally and ended Mauritania's brief democratic experiment.

title: AQIM Kidnaps Western Hostages in Sahara
description: AQIM escalated its campaign by kidnapping multiple Western nationals across the Sahara region in 2008, using Mauritanian territory as a transit zone. The hostage crisis drew international attention and pressured the new military government to confront the jihadist threat.

title: Abdel Aziz Wins Presidential Election After Coup
description: General Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz resigned from the military and won the July 2009 presidential election with 52% of the vote following the Dakar Accord power-sharing deal. The opposition disputed the results but Aziz consolidated power, beginning a decade of strongman rule.

title: Mauritania Severs Diplomatic Ties with Israel
description: In response to Israel's military operation in Gaza, Mauritania recalled its ambassador in January 2009 and expelled Israeli diplomats by March. Full diplomatic relations were formally terminated by March 2010, making Mauritania the first Arab state to reverse normalization with Israel.

title: Joint Military Operation Against AQIM in Mali
description: Mauritania launched cross-border military operations into northern Mali targeting AQIM bases in 2010, marking an aggressive shift in counter-terrorism strategy. The operations, sometimes coordinated with French forces, disrupted jihadist logistics and demonstrated Mauritania's willingness to project force beyond its borders.

title: Last Major Terrorist Attack on Mauritanian Soil
description: A suicide bombing at a military barracks in Nema in February 2011 was the last significant AQIM attack inside Mauritania. The country's combined military, intelligence, and ideological counter-terrorism approach succeeded in suppressing domestic jihadist activity where neighbors failed.

title: Sahel Crisis Spills Over from Mali Collapse
description: The collapse of the Malian state in 2012 following a Tuareg rebellion and jihadist takeover of the north sent thousands of refugees into southeastern Mauritania. The Mbera refugee camp near the border grew to host over 50,000 Malian refugees, straining local resources.

title: Abdel Aziz Re-elected with Expanded Majority
description: President Abdel Aziz won re-election in June 2014 with 82% of the vote in an election boycotted by major opposition parties. His dominance consolidated single-party rule under the Union for the Republic (UPR), marginalizing political opposition.

title: G5 Sahel Regional Security Alliance Established
description: Mauritania co-founded the G5 Sahel alliance in February 2014 with Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, and Chad, headquartered in Nouakchott. The organization aimed to coordinate regional security and development responses to terrorism, trafficking, and instability across the Sahel.

title: IRA Anti-Slavery Activists Sentenced to Prison
description: Thirteen members of the Initiative for the Resurgence of the Abolitionist Movement (IRA) led by Biram Dah Abeid were sentenced to up to 15 years in prison after anti-slavery protests. The harsh sentences drew international condemnation and highlighted the government's repression of abolitionist activism.

title: Strengthened Anti-Slavery Legislation Enacted
description: Mauritania passed a new anti-slavery law in August 2015 expanding the definition of slavery to include forced labor and child exploitation, and increasing penalties for offenders. Despite the legal progress, only a handful of prosecutions had occurred by the time of passage.

title: Severe Drought Triggers Food Crisis
description: A severe drought across the Sahel in 2015 left over 600,000 Mauritanians food insecure, devastating pastoral communities dependent on livestock. The crisis accelerated rural-to-urban migration and highlighted the country's extreme vulnerability to climate-driven shocks.

title: Constitutional Referendum Abolishes Senate
description: A constitutional referendum on 5 August 2017 abolished the Senate and replaced the national flag, adding two red stripes to honor soldiers who died defending the country. The opposition denounced the referendum as an Abdel Aziz power grab designed to eliminate a check on presidential authority.

title: Greater Tortue Ahmeyim Gas Project FID Approved
description: BP and Kosmos Energy took the final investment decision on the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) LNG project straddling the Mauritania-Senegal maritime border in December 2018. With estimated reserves of 1,400 billion cubic meters, GTA promised to transform Mauritania into a major gas exporter.

title: Ghazouani Wins Presidency in First Peaceful Transfer
description: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani, Abdel Aziz's handpicked successor, won the June 2019 presidential election with 52% of the vote. The transfer marked the first peaceful transition between elected presidents in Mauritania's history, though both were former army generals from the same ruling party.

title: Post-Election Ethnic Protests and Internet Shutdown
description: Disputed election results in June 2019 triggered protests by Black Mauritanian communities alleging ethnic discrimination in voter registration and results. The government imposed a weeks-long internet blackout and arrested opposition supporters, drawing condemnation from human rights organizations.

title: Abdel Aziz Arrested on Corruption Charges
description: Former President Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz was placed under investigation and later arrested on charges of corruption, money laundering, and illicit enrichment during his decade in power. The prosecution marked an unprecedented move against a former head of state in Mauritania.

title: COVID-19 Economic Emergency and Debt Relief
description: Mauritania declared a state of emergency in March 2020 as COVID-19 disrupted fishing exports and mining revenue, the two largest economic sectors. The country received IMF emergency financing and G20 debt service suspension to manage the fiscal shock.

title: EU Renews Fisheries Partnership Agreement
description: The EU and Mauritania signed a renewed Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement protocol in November 2021 worth approximately 60 million euros annually. The deal remained controversial for its impact on artisanal fishers and concerns about overfishing of small pelagic stocks.

title: G5 Sahel Joint Force Weakened by Regional Coups
description: Military coups in Mali and Chad in 2020-2021 undermined the G5 Sahel joint force, with Mauritania left as the most stable founding member. Mali's withdrawal from the organization in 2022 and Burkina Faso's coup further eroded the regional security architecture Mauritania had championed.

title: Abdel Aziz Convicted and Sentenced to Prison
description: A Nouakchott criminal court convicted former President Abdel Aziz of illicit enrichment and corruption in December 2023, sentencing him to five years in prison. The trial was the first criminal conviction of a former head of state in Mauritania and West Africa.

title: Severe Sahel Drought Displaces Pastoral Communities
description: Prolonged drought across the Sahel in 2023 left over 900,000 Mauritanians facing food insecurity, with pastoral regions in the east and south hardest hit. Desertification continued to consume agricultural land at accelerating rates, compounding the effects of climate change.

title: EU Signs 210 Million Euro Migration Partnership
description: The European Commission signed a migration partnership with Mauritania worth over 210 million euros in February 2024, aimed at curbing Atlantic route migration to the Canary Islands. The deal positioned Mauritania as a key EU border externalization partner amid surging migrant arrivals.

title: Ghazouani Re-elected for Second Presidential Term
description: President Mohamed Ould Ghazouani won re-election in June 2024 with over 56% of the vote, securing a second and constitutionally final term. Opposition candidates alleged fraud, but international observers noted a broadly orderly process.

title: First Gas Flows at Greater Tortue Ahmeyim
description: The Greater Tortue Ahmeyim LNG project achieved first gas on 31 December 2024, with BP operating the deepest subsea development in Africa at 2,850 meters depth. Phase 1 is expected to produce 2.3 million tonnes of LNG annually, positioning Mauritania as a significant energy exporter.
